reasons: The rendered redline is identical to the original text — the promised clarifying insertion of the numeral ("ninety (90) days" in § 19.2) does not actually appear, and no comment was generated, so the finding is a no-op and not actionable.

On the rationale's own analysis the warranty package meets the preferred position (professional/workmanlike + material conformance in § 19.1, 90-day Deliverable conformance and term-long Hosted Services conformance in § 19.2, law-compliance and no-malicious-code in § 19.3, repair/replace/re-perform escalating to termination and refund in § 19.4, and a disclaimer in § 19.5 that expressly does not limit express warranties). The correct classification is therefore 'compliant', with the 'Fees paid' vs 'paid or payable' point noted in the rationale rather than surfaced for review.

The only stated basis for review is that the period is spelled in words rather than numerals. That is a cosmetic drafting/verification artifact, not a material term under the WARRANTY rule, and the playbook directs that sub-preferred or immaterial drafting points be noted, not flagged.

The failed deterministic check ('warranty period ≥ 90 days') is a false negative caused by the spelled-out phrase "For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later"; it is a phrasing variant and does not evidence a short or missing period.
